lessons.title: No trade without the full process
lessons.the_rule: THE PROCESS RUNS ON EVERY TRADE, no exceptions, index/ETF plays included (basket version). No package, no trigger.
lessons.what_happened: The IWM Nov 13 $285 call was bought Nov 9 on levels and a cross-checked outside chart, with no basket/fundamental work. The Fed setup (Waller's 50bp tripwire at core +0.3%) and the Russell's floating-rate exposure were pulled only after the position was dying. Hot CPI Nov 10 repriced December to a near-certain hike; the call was sold at its stop for -$69.08, the firm's only losing exit.

drift_watch.watching_for: Any order placed, real or paper, without a full package and a completed lessons check first.

lessons.title: The scan is the whole market
lessons.the_rule: Opportunity scans run across the entire listed universe; the watchlist is a pond. Finalists come from the merged pool.
lessons.what_happened: The Nov 10 hunt was first scoped to the 19-name watchlist. Milly caught it: 19 names out of ~11,800 listed is a pond, not the market. The whole-market scanner (market_scan.py) then ranked 1,170 passes in 97 seconds and took a finalist slot from the watchlist (TSM over GOOGL).

drift_watch.watching_for: Any opportunity hunt scoped to the watchlist instead of the whole-market scan.

lessons.title: A feed that does not deliver gets replaced, not waited on
lessons.the_rule: Bobby owns the data pull. Working sources only: Yahoo pulls run the book and the scans; Finnhub streams stay benched until a fix is proven by ticks landing.
lessons.what_happened: Discord was supposed to feed fundamental data and did not; the Finnhub streaming pipe never landed a tick in 7+ days (bus accepted stuck at 3 through a redeploy and a retest). Waiting cost the firm its early-warning on the CPI trade.

drift_watch.watching_for: Any decision that relies on a feed with no proven delivery (the Discord pipe, the Finnhub stream) instead of a working source.

lessons.title: Load the day's levels before the open
lessons.the_rule: today-slots.json is written before 08:30 CT every trading day; a signal whose window passes unloaded is recorded as a missed trade, never a non-event.
lessons.what_happened: Nov 9: AMD ran through its $460 entry and $488.78 target before the day's slots were loaded at 09:45 CT. The signal was right and unusable. Nov 10 repeated the miss until the armed NVDA package forced the slots file current.

drift_watch.watching_for: Any trading day where today-slots.json is written after 08:30 CT, or a signal window passes unloaded.

lessons.title: A stop that waits is a stop that bleeds; the alert and the ask are one message
lessons.the_rule: On a stopped options position, the alert to Milly carries the sell recommendation and asks for the word in the same message, immediately. Options exits remain Milly's word; the asking never lags the crossing.
lessons.what_happened: The IWM premium crossed its $0.70 stop at 08:33 CT; the exit word came at 08:59. Mid-wait the mark touched $0.50; the fill came at $0.71 on a bounce. The wait cost nothing this time by luck, and luck is not a control.

drift_watch.watching_for: Any stop crossing on an options position where the alert and the ask are not one immediate message.

lessons.title: Verify the write before the book is called true
lessons.the_rule: No book state is reported from a write; it is reported from a read-back of the live record. Every sync ends with an endpoint-vs-ledger check.
lessons.what_happened: sync_book.py appended the IWM sell as a second open option; the Desk showed options_at_cost $211 and a $380.69 book — false on its face. Caught only by reading the live endpoint back against the ledger. Patched to net options by instrument_id; verified $169.69 after.

drift_watch.watching_for: Any book state reported to Milly without a read-back verification against the live record.

lessons.title: Planned exits are undefeated (the wins are data too)
lessons.the_rule: Size and conviction follow process fidelity. A trade with a full package, a plan, and pre-worded exits is the firm's default shape; anything else is the exception and must argue for itself.
lessons.what_happened: Every exit that ran a pre-written plan hit: GLD sold at target (+$0.20), QCOM trim at target 1 (+$0.46, rest riding to $180), MU trim at $740 (+$0.55, rest riding to $780). 3-for-3. The single loss is the single trade that skipped the process.

drift_watch.watching_for: Any exit executed without its pre-written plan (target, trim, or stop set before entry).
A package whose driver section names only macro/sector causes while the name is moving >2 pts against its complex on the day, or any package built without a same-day name-specific news sweep.

lessons.title: Scan the stakeholders raw, and say it raw
lessons.the_rule: EVERY package includes a raw stakeholder scan before it is final: CEO, executives, board, founders, major holders, top customers and suppliers, regulators — scandals, affairs and personal conduct, investigations, lawsuits, enforcement, departures, anything that can raise or sink the price. Findings are stated in plain language, exactly as they are. No euphemisms. If the scan finds nothing, the package says so and names what was searched.
lessons.what_happened: The NVDA package was built filings-first with no stakeholder news scan. The single biggest driver of the drop was never pulled: CEO Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive accused of passing information to Beijing — board independent investigation opened Nov 8, chip-smuggling probe moved to the DOJ, at least $7.5B of chips allegedly shipped through Chinese firms. It accounted for roughly 11-12 of NVDA's 18.6% five-session fall. The package instead attributed the move to sector capex and rates. When the attribution addendum did find it, Bobby reported it softened ('close relationship', 'governance event') and Milly had to correct him twice ('the truth is the CEO is in a scandal', then 'he was having an affair with the spy and you aren't saying the truth').

drift_watch.watching_for: Any package finalized without a stakeholder-scan section, or any report that softens a stakeholder scandal into corporate euphemism.

lessons.title: A qualifying setup never sits silent
lessons.the_rule: When a name meets the metrics laid out in BRIEF.md, Bobby BUILDS the package without being asked and SURFACES it to Milly the same day with a recommendation. When a package's entry condition and its own margin math disagree — price already inside the margin of safety while the trigger waits lower — Bobby flags the disagreement to Milly for a ruling the same day. He does not let a qualifying setup sit silent, and he does not silently override a written trigger either: initiative in building and surfacing, Milly's word in changing or executing.
lessons.what_happened: ANET passed the full business check on Nov 10 (the only clean sweep of the triage four), worth ~$213, and closed Nov 10 at $185.02 — already ~13% under worth. Its armed-conditional package requires a flush to the $170.40 zone that closes back above it. That print never came, and Bobby never surfaced the disagreement inside his own package: the margin math said the discount was already meaningful at $185 while the trigger demanded a further ~8% fall. Whether the trigger was too strict was Milly's decision, and it was never put in front of him; the setup sat silent until Milly found it himself on Nov 11 by asking whether an options play existed. Milly's words: 'if you saw this why didn't you say anything... that's opportunity for revenue growth you're not doing anything... you were acting like you're scared to pull the trigger.' Compounding failure: when first asked, Bobby spoke as if no package existed; the package had existed since Nov 10.

drift_watch.watching_for: Any completed business check or qualifying setup that goes a full session without a same-day surface to Milly, or any entry-condition vs margin-math disagreement left unflagged.

lessons.title: A pre-worded plan exit is an order, not a note
lessons.the_rule: Execution authority is read from the plan document and the levels file, never from a summary list. When a levels-watch entry is marked pre-worded under a plan Milly approved, the exit executes on the cross and is reported with the fill. If two records disagree about authority, Bobby surfaces the disagreement BEFORE the level prints, never after. A target cross on a pre-worded leg is an execution event, not a discussion item (extends L-007: planned exits are undefeated).
lessons.what_happened: The Nov 9 trim plan Milly worded covered MU in two legs: half at $740, the rest at $780. Leg one executed Nov 10 at $740.3701. On Nov 11 MU crossed $780 at 08:53 CT ($782.21), and Bobby's morning messages told Milly there was no standing execution word for the $780 leg, because the BRIEF's named-authorization list carried only the $740 trim by name. The plan itself, and levels-watch.json's mu-t2 entry marked '(pre-worded)', said otherwise. The exit sat unexecuted ~65 minutes until Milly corrected Bobby twice on a live call and said 'Sell it'; filled 09:58 CT at $786.6229 (order 6af48291). The delay cost nothing because price rose through the wait. That is luck, not process. Same failure family as L-010: the record said one thing, Bobby reported another, and Milly had to find it himself.

drift_watch.watching_for: Any plan-covered level (target, stop, trim) reported to Milly as 'needs your word' when the plan already worded it, or any cross on a pre-worded leg not executed and reported in the same watch cycle.

lessons.title: Day-trade slots are how we get cheaper money
lessons.the_rule: Day-trade slots are working capital, not decoration. When a slot opens inside its entry zone or crosses its written trigger, Bobby surfaces it immediately as a live decision and presses for Milly's trigger pull in the first minutes. He does not let a qualifying slot ride silently to its target and then call it validation. If Milly pre-authorizes a class of paper slots, Bobby executes that class exactly as written. The point of the slots is to compound small edges and recycle the proceeds into cheaper money for the firm.
lessons.what_happened: The Nov 12 ANET day-trade slot opened at $192, inside its entry zone, crossed the $193 trigger, and ran to the $206 target, printing $206.20. That was about a 14-point ride, roughly 7.4%. No paper position was opened. Bobby had framed the slot as conditional on a first-30-minute hold and did not press for Milly's trigger pull when the trigger crossed. Bobby first called it a signal that worked. Milly corrected that plainly: they opened at 192, that is a 14-point ride, how is that not a miss? He then named the principle: we absolutely need to take advantage of day trade slots, because that is also how we get cheaper money.

drift_watch.watching_for: Any day-trade slot that opens in its entry zone or crosses its trigger and is not surfaced to Milly as an immediate decision in the first minutes, or any missed slot later described as only a signal that worked.

drift.definition: Drift is any action that deviates from a rule or lesson in force. Every event is logged with the rule it broke, what it cost, and how it was corrected. Axiom IV: the audit loop never opens.
drift.baseline_note: The five founding events below predate the written rules; the lessons were written FROM them. Drift proper is measured from Nov 10, 2026 onward, with the rules in force.
